domain_label: DTC Plated-Jewelry Pricing, Contribution Margin & Value-Engineering Reprice
purpose: A method for turning a per-piece landed COGS for a plated fashion-jewelry SKU into a defensible DTC retail price by placing the price between a contribution-margin floor and a measured willingness-to-pay ceiling inside a real competitor price band, and for deciding when a lower price is a margin-sacrificing discount versus a permanent value-engineering reprice that cuts COGS while holding perceived quality, with every market number tagged [FACT]/[METHOD]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] and no price ever stated as measured that was not measured.
assumptions: the per-piece landed COGS is inherited as a labelled band from the sibling kb1_cogs_and_landed segment (base metal + gold/rhodium plating consumption + findings + labor + packaging + freight/duty), not re-derived here; its width propagates into every margin band

keystone markup (retailer doubles cost to set retail; 'keystone' = a 2.0x cost multiplier, i.e. ~50% gross margin on price) is a real, well-established retail-pricing convention [FACT-retail-pricing]; that fashion/costume jewelry frequently runs multiples well above keystone (roughly 3-5x+ cost) is an [ESTIMATE] not a measured figure

contribution margin per unit = price - variable cost per unit, and contribution-margin ratio = contribution margin / price, are cost-accounting identities [FACT-managerial-accounting]; they are computed, never guessed

fashion/costume jewelry is priced substantially on perceived value / willingness-to-pay, not on material cost, because material cost is a small fraction of a low-ticket impulse accessory [ESTIMATE-market-structure, MED]; the actual WTP for the owner's SKUs is [UNKNOWN] until measured

any specific retail price, competitor price, price band, discount elasticity, or willingness-to-pay figure is NOT fabricated here; the KB encodes the METHOD to measure or pull each (Van Westendorp PSM, Gabor-Granger, conjoint/MaxDiff, A/B price tests, public storefront band-mapping) and marks the number [UNKNOWN] until produced

US FTC Guides Against Deceptive Pricing (16 CFR Part 233) constrain former-price / comparative 'was/now' and list-price discount claims; a 'sale' must reference a bona fide former price [FACT-16CFR233]

marketing / customer-acquisition cost (CAC) is deliberately excluded from the contribution-margin-before-marketing computed here and is owned by the sibling kb3_viability_cac_ltv segment; this KB stops at the priced SKU and its unit contribution and hands off
exclusions: re-deriving the per-piece landed COGS (that is kb1_cogs_and_landed; this KB accepts its band as input)
CAC, AOV, repeat/LTV, payback period, break-even units and the go/no-go verdict (that is kb3_viability_cac_ltv; this KB delivers unit contribution and stops before CAC)

the material/finish cost levers themselves (base-metal choice, plating micron thickness, barrier layers, findings) which are owned by the materials specialist S2 kb3_quality_cost_value_engineering; this KB consumes their COGS-reduction result as the value-engineering input
the poll/survey instrument mechanics and sampling-bias correction (owned by the poll specialist S4); this KB names which price-discovery instrument to use and why, not how to field it
asserting a specific US market price, competitor brand price, gold-plated-vs-solid share, or demographic willingness-to-pay as a measured fact
tax, sales-tax nexus, or accounting/legal advice for a specific filing

competency_questions.question: What is keystone markup, how does it differ from margin, and why is a cost-multiple alone not a defensible price for fashion jewelry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KEYSTONE_MARKUP_FACT defines keystone as a 2.0x cost multiplier [FACT] and notes fashion-jewelry multiples run higher [ESTIMATE], and MARGIN_VS_MARKUP shows markup-on-cost vs margin-on-price arithmetic, with FASHION_PRICE_CONTEXT explaining why material cost is a weak price anchor for a low-ticket accessory

competency_questions.question: How is per-unit contribution margin computed for a plated-jewelry SKU, and exactly which costs are variable versus excluded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRIBUTION_MARGIN_MATH states CM = price - variable cost and CM ratio = CM/price [FACT], and VARIABLE_COST_SCOPE enumerates landed COGS + payment fees + pick/pack + returns/shrink reserve as variable while excluding CAC and fixed overhead (contribution-before-marketing)

competency_questions.question: What is perceived-value (value-based) pricing for fashion jewelry and which value levers move willingness-to-pay?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERCEIVED_VALUE_PRICING states price is set to willingness-to-pay via reference price, price-quality signalling, materials story (vermeil/rhodium), packaging and brand, and FASHION_PRICE_CONTEXT grounds why an impulse accessory is priced on value not material cost

competency_questions.question: How is willingness-to-pay measured honestly rather than guessed, and what biases threaten each instrument?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WTP_MEASUREMENT names Van Westendorp PSM, Gabor-Granger, conjoint/MaxDiff and live A/B price tests [METHOD], flags stated-vs-revealed preference and self-selection/incentive bias, and marks the resulting WTP figure [UNKNOWN] until measured

competency_questions.question: How is a SKU placed in a price band and price point, and how is the competitor band built without inventing prices?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICE_BAND_PLACEMENT builds the entry/hero/premium tier ladder from a public-storefront band map [METHOD] and CHARM_PRICE_POINTS applies psychological price endings and good-better-best anchoring [FACT-effect, ESTIMATE-magnitude]

competency_questions.question: What is the step-by-step method to set a defensible retail price for one SKU?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFENSIBLE_PRICE_METHOD sets floor = TARGET_MARGIN_FLOOR (cost + fees + required contribution), ceiling = measured WTP, band = competitor placement, then picks a charm price point inside floor-ceiling-band, refusing to price below the contribution floor

competency_questions.question: How does a DTC operator's margin structure differ from a wholesale/keystone chain, and what does it capture and pay for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DTC_MARGIN_CAPTURE shows the DTC seller captures both the wholesale and retail markup spread (no retailer keystone taken out) but funds CAC and fulfilment out of that spread, so a high gross margin is necessary but not sufficient

competency_questions.question: What does a discount actually do to contribution margin, and how much extra volume must a promo sell to break even?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCOUNT_PROMO_EFFECT states that a price discount comes entirely out of contribution so a small % off price is a large % off margin, computes the break-even volume lift = discount/(CM ratio - discount), and PROMO_MARGIN_TRAP names reference-price erosion and promo dependency plus FTC 16 CFR 233 former-price limits

competency_questions.question: When is a lower price a value-engineering job (cut COGS, hold quality and margin) rather than a discount (sacrifice margin)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VALUE_ENGINEERING_LINK pulls the S2 COGS-reduction levers (base metal, plating micron, findings, batch/MOQ) to lower the price floor while holding perceived quality, and DISCOUNT_VS_VE_DECISION gives the rule that classifies a price cut as a temporary discount vs a permanent value-engineered reprice before acting

competency_questions.question: Why is realized margin lower than list margin, and how are returns, exchanges and shrink carried?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURNS_REALIZED_MARGIN separates list/nominal contribution from realized contribution after a returns/refurbish/shrink/chargeback reserve, and states the reserve is measured or estimated per category, never omitted

competency_questions.question: How is honesty discipline enforced so that firm margin math is trusted while every price/WTP/competitor number stays labelled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] identities (keystone, CM math, FTC pricing rule) from the [METHOD] price-discovery instruments and the [UNKNOWN] WTP/competitor prices, and flags any single-point price as an illustration until measured

competency_questions.question: What does the pricing segment hand to the viability and assortment layers, and what stays out of scope?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICING_HANDOFF delivers the defensible price and unit contribution-before-marketing per SKU with its floor/ceiling/band conditions, the discount policy and the value-engineering reprice option, and stops cleanly before CAC/LTV/break-even

glossary.definition: The retail convention of doubling cost to set price: keystone = a 2.0x cost multiplier, equivalent to a 50% gross margin on the retail price [FACT-retail-pricing]. Fashion/costume jewelry is commonly marked up well above keystone (roughly 3-5x+ cost) because material cost is a small share of a perceived-value accessory [ESTIMATE]; the exact multiple for the owner's SKUs is [UNKNOWN] until priced against measured willingness-to-pay.

Markup is profit expressed as a percentage of COST (retail = cost x (1 + markup)); margin is profit expressed as a percentage of PRICE (margin = (price - cost)/price). A 2.0x keystone is a 100% markup on cost but a 50% margin on price; confusing the two systematically under-prices, so every price statement fixes which base it uses [FACT-managerial-accounting].

Per-unit contribution margin = price - variable cost per unit; contribution-margin ratio = contribution margin / price. It is the dollars each sale contributes toward fixed cost, CAC and profit after variable cost, and is a cost-accounting identity, not an estimate [FACT-managerial-accounting]. Here it is computed contribution-BEFORE-marketing (CAC excluded, handed to kb3).

For a DTC plated-jewelry SKU: inherited landed COGS + payment-processing fees + pick/pack/ship-supplies + a returns/refurbish/shrink reserve. Excludes fixed overhead and CAC. Only costs that scale with each additional unit sold belong in the contribution-margin denominator [METHOD/FACT].

Setting price to the customer's willingness-to-pay rather than to a cost multiple, using reference price, price-quality signalling, the materials story (e.g. vermeil = >=10k gold >=2.5um over sterling; rhodium-over-silver bright/tarnish-resistant finish), packaging and brand as WTP levers. For a low-ticket impulse accessory this typically yields a higher, more defensible price than cost-plus [ESTIMATE-market-structure]; the WTP level is [UNKNOWN] until measured.

Instruments that estimate WTP instead of guessing it: Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter (four price-perception questions bracketing an acceptable range), Gabor-Granger (buy-intent at stepped prices), conjoint/MaxDiff (trade-off-based feature+price valuation), and live A/B price tests (revealed preference). All are [METHOD]; stated-preference instruments overstate WTP and are subject to self-selection and incentive bias, so revealed-preference A/B tests are the strongest signal.

A price band is the tier range a SKU competes in (entry / hero / premium), built by mapping public competitor storefront prices [METHOD] rather than inventing them; a price point is the specific charm-priced figure chosen inside the band (psychological endings, good-better-best anchoring). Band placement signals quality tier; the wrong band mis-signals regardless of the number.

A discount lowers price while COGS is unchanged, so the entire cut comes out of contribution margin (a margin sacrifice, often reference-price-eroding). A value-engineering reprice lowers the COGS floor first (base-metal choice, plating micron tuning, barrier layers, findings, batch/MOQ from S2) so a lower price can be held permanently WITHOUT lowering margin or perceived quality. The two must be classified before acting; they are opposite operations.

List (nominal) contribution uses the full price; realized contribution nets out returns/exchanges, refurbishment/write-off of returned plated pieces, shrink and payment chargebacks. Realized margin is always <= list margin; carrying a returns/shrink reserve per category keeps the priced SKU honest [METHOD/ESTIMATE].

The FTC Guides Against Deceptive Pricing require that a 'was/now', 'list price' or comparative-price claim reference a bona fide former or prevailing price at which the item was actually offered; a fictitious former price used to manufacture a discount is deceptive [FACT-16CFR233]. This binds how promos and reference prices may be advertised.

nodes.definition: Accept the per-piece landed COGS band for each plated-jewelry SKU from the sibling kb1_cogs_and_landed segment as the input this KB prices on top of, without re-deriving it: base metal (brass/925/316L) + gold/rhodium plating consumption (driven by micron thickness and surface area) + findings + labor + packaging + inbound freight/duty, delivered as a labelled [ESTIMATE] band whose width is dominated by plating thickness, base-metal choice and MOQ. This landed number is the hard floor under every price and the denominator input to contribution margin; its band width propagates into every margin band, so the pricing work states its uncertainty rather than inventing a tight COGS point.

included: the per-SKU landed COGS band as accepted input
plating micron / base metal / MOQ as the width drivers
landed COGS as the price floor and CM denominator input
excluded: payment fees, pick/pack and returns reserve (VARIABLE_COST_SCOPE)

pros.claim: Taking kb1's landed band as a labelled input keeps the margin model honest about where its uncertainty originates instead of inventing a tighter COGS
pros.example: carrying a $2.20-3.80 landed band for a rhodium-plated 925 ring makes the resulting margin band traceable to plating micron, not to false precision

cons.claim: A wide landed band caps how tight any margin or floor can be, so precision is blocked one layer up
cons.example: no pricing refinement narrows the CM band while the plating-thickness cost stays a band

failure_modes: treating a band-centre landed point as a measured cost and propagating false precision into margin
re-deriving landed COGS here and double-counting kb1's work
acceptance_tests: the per-SKU landed COGS is stated as an accepted [ESTIMATE] band with plating micron / base metal / MOQ named as width drivers and identified as the price floor and CM denominator input
revisit_triggers: kb1 republishes the landed COGS band
a live plating-run or MOQ quote tightens the landed band
a base-metal or micron spec change moves COGS

base.update_signal: the inherited landed COGS band or its plating/MOQ drivers change

nodes.definition: Establish the market-structure context that governs how a plated fashion/costume piece is priced, distinct from fine jewelry. Fashion/costume jewelry is a low-ticket, high-frequency impulse accessory where material cost is a small fraction of retail, so price is set substantially on perceived value / willingness-to-pay rather than on a metal-content cost-plus formula [ESTIMATE-market-structure, MED] - the opposite of fine gold jewelry priced near spot + making charge. This context is why keystone/cost-plus is a floor check, not the price, and why the whole KB leans on WTP measurement and band placement. Elasticity, reference price and the accessory/gifting occasion shape the ceiling; the actual elasticity for the owner's SKUs is [UNKNOWN] until tested.

included: fashion/costume vs fine-jewelry price structure
material cost as a small share of a perceived-value accessory
why cost-plus is a floor not the price

pros.claim: Naming fashion jewelry as perceived-value-priced stops the venture from anchoring the whole price on a cost multiple
pros.example: recognising that a $4 landed piece can defensibly retail far above 4x cost reframes pricing from cost-plus to value-based

cons.claim: The perceived-value structure is an [ESTIMATE] about the category, so it guides the approach but does not itself set any number
cons.example: a commodity look-alike SKU may in fact be near-commodity-priced, closer to cost-plus

failure_modes: pricing a fashion accessory on metal-content cost-plus as if it were fine jewelry
treating the perceived-value structure as a licence to invent a WTP number
acceptance_tests: the fashion/costume-vs-fine price structure, material cost as a small perceived-value share, and cost-plus-as-floor-not-price are stated with the [ESTIMATE] tag and [UNKNOWN] elasticity
revisit_triggers: a live elasticity or WTP test result lands for a SKU
the SKU mix shifts toward near-commodity look-alikes
a category demand read (S1) updates the tier structure

base.update_signal: a category elasticity or tier-structure read changes

nodes.definition: State the keystone convention as a real, load-bearing [FACT] and bound it honestly. Keystone markup = doubling cost to set price, i.e. a 2.0x cost multiplier, equivalent to a 50% gross margin on the retail price [FACT-retail-pricing]. Traditional two-step wholesale-to-retail (manufacturer keystones to wholesale, retailer keystones again) implies roughly a 4x cost retail. Fashion/costume jewelry is commonly marked up ABOVE keystone (roughly 3-5x+ cost) because perceived value, not metal content, sets the ceiling [ESTIMATE, MED - directional, not a measured figure for the owner's SKUs]. Keystone is used here as a fast floor/sanity multiple, never as the final price: the defensible price is the WTP-and-band price bounded below by the contribution floor.

included: keystone = 2.0x cost = 50% margin [FACT]
two-step ~4x cost retail convention
fashion-jewelry above-keystone multiples as [ESTIMATE]
excluded: the DTC capture of both markups (DTC_MARGIN_CAPTURE)

pros.claim: Carrying keystone as a labelled [FACT] gives a fast, defensible floor multiple without pretending it is the final price
pros.example: a keystone 2x on a $3 landed piece flags $6 as a bare floor, immediately shown as too low for a perceived-value accessory

cons.claim: Stating jewelry multiples above keystone as [ESTIMATE] can read as vague to someone wanting a fixed multiplier
cons.example: a stakeholder wanting '5x cost' as a rule must accept it as directional, not measured

failure_modes: treating keystone (or any fixed multiple) as the final price instead of a floor check
presenting the above-keystone fashion multiple as a measured fact rather than an [ESTIMATE]
acceptance_tests: keystone = 2.0x cost = 50% margin is stated as [FACT], the ~4x two-step convention is noted, and fashion-jewelry above-keystone multiples are tagged [ESTIMATE] and never used as the final price
revisit_triggers: a measured competitor multiple or WTP result lands
the landed COGS input changes the floor multiple
a channel change (adding wholesale) alters the markup chain

base.update_signal: a measured multiple, WTP result, or channel change updates the markup convention

nodes.definition: Fix the arithmetic that a keystone/markup instinct most often gets wrong: markup is profit as a percentage of COST (retail = cost x (1 + markup%)), while margin is profit as a percentage of PRICE (margin% = (price - cost)/price). A 2.0x keystone is a 100% markup on cost but only a 50% margin on price; a 3x cost is a 200% markup but a ~66.7% margin. Confusing the two systematically under-prices (a '50% markup' set as if it were a 50% margin leaves cost at two-thirds of price, not half). Every price statement in this KB fixes which base it uses, and margin is the base for all contribution math because CM ratio is defined on price [FACT-managerial-accounting].

included: markup-on-cost vs margin-on-price formulas
the keystone 100% markup = 50% margin equivalence
margin as the base for contribution math

pros.claim: Pinning the markup-vs-margin distinction prevents a whole class of systematic under-pricing errors
pros.example: converting a target 60% margin to the correct 2.5x cost multiple avoids the '60% markup' mistake that leaves too little margin

cons.claim: The distinction is arithmetic bookkeeping, so over-emphasising it can distract from the harder WTP/band judgement
cons.example: getting the conversion exactly right still says nothing about what customers will pay

failure_modes: setting a markup percentage as if it were a margin percentage and under-pricing
mixing cost-based and price-based percentages within one contribution model
acceptance_tests: markup = profit/cost and margin = profit/price are both stated, the keystone 100%-markup = 50%-margin equivalence is shown, and margin is fixed as the base for contribution math
revisit_triggers: a downstream model is found expressing a margin target as a markup
the target-margin floor is recomputed
a channel adds a wholesale markup step

base.update_signal: a margin/markup conversion error or a channel markup change is found

nodes.definition: Define and compute the core identity the whole segment turns on: per-unit contribution margin (CM) = price - variable cost per unit; contribution-margin ratio = CM / price. CM is the dollars each sale contributes toward fixed cost, CAC and profit after covering variable cost, and it is an accounting identity, not an estimate [FACT-managerial-accounting]. This KB computes contribution-BEFORE-marketing: CAC is deliberately excluded and handed to kb3, so the CM here is the pool CAC and fixed cost are later paid out of. Worked shape: a SKU priced $P with variable cost $V has CM = P-V and CM ratio (P-V)/P; the CM ratio, not the gross dollar, is what the discount and break-even math key off.

included: CM = price - variable cost and CM ratio = CM/price [FACT]
contribution-before-marketing (CAC excluded)
the CM ratio as the key for discount/break-even math

pros.claim: Grounding the segment on the CM identity makes every downstream pricing and discount decision auditable arithmetic
pros.example: a $18 price on $6 variable cost gives CM $12 and a 0.667 CM ratio that the discount math then keys off directly

cons.claim: CM-before-marketing looks healthier than the after-CAC reality, so it must be labelled to avoid over-optimism
cons.example: a 0.667 CM ratio can still lose money once CAC is loaded in kb3

failure_modes: reading contribution-before-marketing as final profit and ignoring the CAC handed to kb3
putting fixed cost into the per-unit variable term and understating CM
acceptance_tests: CM = price - variable cost and CM ratio = CM/price are stated as [FACT], contribution-before-marketing (CAC excluded) is declared, and the CM ratio is identified as the key for discount/break-even math
revisit_triggers: the variable-cost scope or landed COGS input changes
kb3 changes how CAC is loaded onto contribution
a price change re-computes the CM ratio

base.update_signal: the variable-cost scope, landed COGS, or CAC-loading convention changes

nodes.definition: Fix exactly which costs belong in the per-unit variable term so the CM ratio is honest. Variable cost per unit for a DTC plated-jewelry SKU = inherited landed COGS (LANDED_COST_INPUT) + payment-processing fees (a % of price + a fixed per-transaction fee, so partly price-scaling) + pick/pack labour and shipping supplies + outbound shipping if not fully customer-paid + a returns/refurbish/shrink reserve (RETURNS_REALIZED_MARGIN). Excluded from variable cost: fixed overhead (rent, salaries, software) and CAC (owned by kb3). The rule is inclusion-by-scaling: only costs that rise with each additional unit sold go in the denominator; mis-scoping either way distorts the CM ratio and every discount decision built on it [METHOD/FACT].

included: landed COGS + payment fees + pick/pack + returns/shrink reserve as variable
the inclusion-by-scaling rule
fixed overhead and CAC excluded

pros.claim: A precise variable-cost scope keeps the CM ratio and every discount/break-even figure trustworthy
pros.example: including the ~3% + $0.30 payment fee and a returns reserve prevents a CM ratio that looks better than reality

cons.claim: Some costs (payment fees fixed component, partial shipping) are only semi-variable, so the scope needs judgement not a clean rule
cons.example: the fixed per-transaction fee is unit-variable but not price-variable, complicating the CM ratio at low prices

failure_modes: smuggling fixed overhead or CAC into variable cost and understating CM
omitting payment fees or the returns reserve and overstating CM
acceptance_tests: variable cost is enumerated as landed COGS + payment fees + pick/pack + returns/shrink reserve with fixed overhead and CAC excluded, governed by the inclusion-by-scaling rule
revisit_triggers: payment-processor rates or shipping policy change
the returns/shrink reserve is re-measured
a cost is reclassified between fixed and variable

base.update_signal: a payment/shipping rate, returns reserve, or cost reclassification changes

nodes.definition: Establish how the owner's DTC/headless-storefront model changes the margin arithmetic versus a wholesale-to-retail chain. Selling direct, the venture captures BOTH the manufacturer-to-wholesale and the wholesale-to-retail keystone spreads (no retailer takes a keystone out), so the gross margin on a direct sale is structurally far above a wholesale margin - the whole reason DTC can price attractively and still profit. But that captured spread is not free: it must fund CAC (paid to Meta/TikTok in place of a retailer's shelf), fulfilment, returns and overhead. So a high DTC gross margin is necessary but not sufficient; the contribution-before-marketing computed here is exactly the pool kb3's CAC is subtracted from. This node reframes 'keystone' from a chain of resellers into a single captured spread the DTC operator spends down.

included: DTC captures both wholesale and retail markup spreads
the captured spread funds CAC, fulfilment, returns, overhead
high gross margin necessary not sufficient

pros.claim: Framing DTC as capturing both markups explains the structural margin headroom the venture prices into
pros.example: a piece that would wholesale at 2x and retail at 4x can be sold direct at ~4x with the full spread retained to fund CAC

cons.claim: The captured-spread framing can lull the venture into reading gross margin as profit before CAC is loaded
cons.example: a 70% gross margin can still be unprofitable once a high paid-social CAC eats the spread

failure_modes: reading the captured DTC spread as profit rather than a pool that funds CAC and fulfilment
pricing at a wholesale margin out of habit and leaving the retail spread uncaptured
acceptance_tests: the DTC capture of both markup spreads, the requirement that the spread fund CAC/fulfilment/returns, and the necessary-not-sufficient point are stated
revisit_triggers: the venture adds a wholesale or marketplace channel that re-inserts a reseller markup
CAC economics (kb3) shift materially
the fulfilment/returns cost structure changes

base.update_signal: a channel addition or CAC/fulfilment structure change alters the captured spread

nodes.definition: Define value-based pricing and the levers that move willingness-to-pay for a plated piece. Price is set toward the customer's WTP rather than a cost multiple, and WTP is raised by: reference price (what the piece is implicitly compared to - a fine-jewelry look at a fashion price), price-quality signalling (a higher price itself signals quality for an unverifiable good), the materials story told honestly (vermeil = >=10k gold >=2.5um over sterling per FTC 16 CFR 23; rhodium-over-silver as a hard, bright-white, tarnish-resistant finish), packaging/unboxing, brand and social proof, and bundling/stacking. These are the ceiling-raising levers; the floor is still the contribution constraint. Crucially, value levers are also the alternative to discounting: raising perceived value defends price where cutting it would erode margin. The WTP level itself is [UNKNOWN] until measured.

included: value-based pricing toward WTP
reference price, price-quality signal, materials story, packaging, brand as WTP levers
value levers as the alternative to discounting

pros.claim: Enumerating the WTP levers gives the venture concrete ways to raise the ceiling instead of only competing on price
pros.example: an honest vermeil/rhodium materials story plus premium packaging can lift WTP without touching COGS

cons.claim: Value levers move WTP by an [UNKNOWN] amount, so they inform the approach but do not set a number until tested
cons.example: better packaging plausibly lifts WTP but by how much is unmeasured until an A/B test

failure_modes: over-claiming the materials story (e.g. calling thin gold plating 'vermeil' without meeting the FTC micron/karat threshold)
treating value levers as a licence to state an unmeasured WTP as fact
acceptance_tests: value-based pricing toward WTP and the reference-price / price-quality-signal / honest-materials-story / packaging / brand levers are stated, with WTP marked [UNKNOWN] until measured and materials claims held to FTC 16 CFR 23
revisit_triggers: a WTP or A/B packaging test lands
the materials/finish spec changes what claims are truthful
competitor value-signalling shifts the reference price

base.update_signal: a WTP test, materials-claim change, or competitor value-signal shift occurs

nodes.definition: Encode how to MEASURE willingness-to-pay instead of guessing it, since the WTP ceiling is [UNKNOWN] until produced. Instruments [METHOD]: Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter (four price-perception questions yielding an acceptable-price range and optimal price point), Gabor-Granger (buy-intent at stepped prices to trace a demand/revenue curve), conjoint / MaxDiff (trade-off-based valuation of features + price, the best for a multi-attribute piece), and live A/B price tests on the storefront (revealed preference, the strongest signal). Every stated-preference instrument overstates WTP and is exposed to self-selection and incentive/giveaway bias (directly relevant to the owner's poll-with-free-item plan, S4), so revealed-preference A/B tests dominate when traffic allows. The output is a WTP band with a confidence tag, never a single fabricated price.

included: Van Westendorp, Gabor-Granger, conjoint/MaxDiff, A/B price tests as [METHOD]
stated-vs-revealed preference and self-selection/incentive bias
WTP output as a labelled band
excluded: the value levers WTP responds to (PERCEIVED_VALUE_PRICING)

pros.claim: Naming concrete WTP instruments turns 'what will they pay' from a guess into a measurement plan
pros.example: a Van Westendorp survey plus a live A/B test brackets the acceptable price range instead of inventing one

cons.claim: Stated-preference WTP overstates and A/B tests need traffic, so early WTP bands are wide and low-confidence
cons.example: a survey-only WTP for a pre-launch SKU is a soft band until revealed-preference data arrives

failure_modes: reporting a stated-preference WTP as a hard price without the overstatement/bias caveat
running an incentivised poll and reading the inflated WTP as revealed demand
acceptance_tests: Van Westendorp, Gabor-Granger, conjoint/MaxDiff and A/B price tests are named as [METHOD], stated-vs-revealed and self-selection/incentive bias are flagged, and WTP is output as a labelled band not a fabricated point
revisit_triggers: a WTP survey or A/B price test completes
storefront traffic crosses the threshold to run a revealed-preference test
an incentivised poll's bias is quantified (S4)

base.update_signal: a WTP survey/A/B result or an incentive-bias measurement lands

nodes.definition: Place each SKU in a price band by building a competitor band map from PUBLIC storefront data [METHOD], never from invented prices. Pull comparable listed prices from public marketplaces and storefronts for the same category/finish, cluster them into tiers (entry / hero / premium), and locate where the SKU's quality and value story justify sitting. Band placement is a quality SIGNAL: pricing a rhodium-over-925 piece into the plastic-costume entry band mis-signals and destroys perceived value regardless of margin, while over-banding above the value story kills conversion. The band constrains the price point independently of the contribution floor and the WTP ceiling; all three must agree. Every competitor price used is a pulled public datum with its date, not a claim; the band is [ESTIMATE] from real listings, and absent data it is [UNKNOWN].

included: competitor band map from public storefront listings [METHOD]
entry/hero/premium tier placement as a quality signal
the band as a constraint alongside floor and ceiling

pros.claim: Building the band from public listings places the SKU on real market evidence rather than a guessed tier
pros.example: clustering 20 comparable public listings into entry/hero/premium locates the hero band the SKU should sit in

cons.claim: Public listed prices are pre-discount and self-selected, so the band is an [ESTIMATE] that can misread true transaction prices
cons.example: a competitor's perpetual-sale listing shows a list price no one pays, skewing the band

failure_modes: inventing a competitor price or band instead of pulling and dating public listings
mis-banding a quality piece into a lower tier and destroying its perceived value
acceptance_tests: the competitor band map is built from dated public storefront listings [METHOD], tier placement is treated as a quality signal, and the band is carried as an [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] not a fabricated price
revisit_triggers: a fresh public competitor price pull is run
the SKU's quality/finish tier changes
a competitor repositions its price band

base.update_signal: a competitor price pull or a SKU tier/positioning change occurs

nodes.definition: Choose the specific price point inside the band using psychological-pricing effects that are real in direction though variable in magnitude. Charm pricing (odd endings like $X9 / $X.99) tends to lift conversion versus a round number by signalling value; round/prestige endings ($X0) can signal quality in a premium band; good-better-best anchoring uses a higher-priced decoy to make the hero SKU look reasonable; and left-digit effects make $29 read materially cheaper than $30. These effects exist [FACT-behavioral-pricing] but their size for the owner's SKUs is an [ESTIMATE] to be A/B tested, not a fixed uplift. The chosen point must still sit inside the contribution floor, the WTP ceiling and the competitor band; charm pricing tunes the last digit, it never overrides the three constraints.

included: charm/odd-ending and prestige-ending price points
good-better-best anchoring and left-digit effects
psychological tuning inside floor/ceiling/band

pros.claim: Applying charm/anchoring effects tunes conversion at the chosen price without changing cost or band
pros.example: moving a hero SKU from $30 to $29 captures the left-digit effect while staying in the same band

cons.claim: The magnitude of psychological effects is an [ESTIMATE] and can be over-relied on as if it were a fixed uplift
cons.example: assuming a guaranteed conversion lift from a $.99 ending without testing can disappoint

failure_modes: treating a charm-ending uplift as a fixed measured gain rather than a testable [ESTIMATE]
letting a psychological price point pull the price below the contribution floor
acceptance_tests: charm/prestige endings, good-better-best anchoring and left-digit effects are stated as [FACT]-direction / [ESTIMATE]-magnitude and constrained to sit inside floor, ceiling and band
revisit_triggers: an A/B test measures a price-ending effect for a SKU
the band or floor moves the feasible price-point set
a premium repositioning changes the appropriate ending style

base.update_signal: an A/B price-ending test or a band/floor change updates the price point

nodes.definition: Set the hard price floor: the minimum price at which the SKU still earns the required contribution margin. Floor logic: required CM ratio must cover the pool that pays for CAC + fixed overhead allocation + returns + target profit (with CAC's magnitude owned by kb3 but reserved here so the floor is not set below what CAC will need), so floor price = variable cost / (1 - required CM ratio). This is the constraint that pricing must never break: a price below the contribution floor loses money on every unit and cannot be fixed by volume. The floor is where this KB meets kb3 - if the required CM ratio (driven by CAC) cannot be met at any defensible price, the honest response is a value-engineering reprice or dropping the SKU, not discounting into loss.

included: floor price = variable cost / (1 - required CM ratio)
the required CM ratio reserving CAC + overhead + returns + profit
the floor as the never-break constraint
excluded: the WTP ceiling and band (PERCEIVED_VALUE_PRICING, PRICE_BAND_PLACEMENT)

pros.claim: A computed contribution floor makes 'never price below this' an explicit number rather than a feeling
pros.example: variable cost $6 with a required 0.6 CM ratio sets a $15 floor that no promo may breach

cons.claim: The required CM ratio depends on the [UNKNOWN]-until-kb3 CAC, so the floor is provisional until CAC is measured
cons.example: a higher-than-expected CAC raises the required CM ratio and lifts the floor after the fact

failure_modes: setting the floor without reserving for CAC and later discovering the SKU cannot cover acquisition
treating the floor as the target price rather than the minimum
acceptance_tests: floor price = variable cost / (1 - required CM ratio) is computed, the required CM ratio is shown reserving CAC + overhead + returns + profit, and the floor is declared the never-break constraint
revisit_triggers: kb3 measures or revises CAC and the required CM ratio
the variable-cost scope or landed COGS changes
the target profit or overhead allocation changes

base.update_signal: a CAC revision, variable-cost change, or profit/overhead target change moves the floor

nodes.definition: The central synthesis: the step-by-step method to set a defensible retail price for one SKU. (1) Compute the contribution FLOOR (TARGET_MARGIN_FLOOR) - the minimum that still earns the required margin. (2) Estimate the WTP CEILING (WTP_MEASUREMENT) - the most customers will pay. (3) Build the competitor BAND (PRICE_BAND_PLACEMENT) - the tier the SKU must sit in. (4) The defensible price is a charm-tuned point (CHARM_PRICE_POINTS) inside the intersection of floor, ceiling and band. If floor > ceiling (cannot earn the margin at what customers will pay), do NOT discount into loss: trigger a value-engineering reprice (VALUE_ENGINEERING_LINK) to lower the floor, or drop the SKU. This method is defensible because every bound is traceable to an identity ([FACT]), a measurement ([METHOD]), or a labelled band - never to a single invented price.

included: the floor-ceiling-band-point method
the floor>ceiling -> value-engineer-or-drop branch
traceability of every bound to FACT/METHOD/band

pros.claim: A floor-ceiling-band method yields a price every stakeholder can audit back to its bound
pros.example: a $29 hero price shown to sit above the $15 floor, below the measured WTP ceiling and inside the hero band is defensible on its face

cons.claim: The method is only as firm as its softest input - a wide WTP band leaves a wide defensible range, not one price
cons.example: an unmeasured WTP ceiling makes the feasible price a range until an A/B test tightens it

failure_modes: skipping the floor check and pricing into loss to hit a band or WTP target
discounting into the floor>ceiling gap instead of value-engineering or dropping the SKU
acceptance_tests: the price is set as a charm-tuned point inside the intersection of the computed floor, the measured WTP ceiling and the competitor band, with the floor>ceiling case routed to value-engineering or drop rather than a loss-making discount
revisit_triggers: any bound (floor, WTP ceiling, band) is re-measured
the SKU is value-engineered, moving the floor
a competitor repositioning moves the band

base.update_signal: a floor, WTP ceiling, band, or value-engineering input changes the price

nodes.definition: Compute what a discount actually does to contribution and what volume it must recover. A discount does not touch cost, so the entire price cut comes out of contribution margin: a small percentage off PRICE is a large percentage off MARGIN. Break-even volume-lift identity: to hold total contribution, required unit-sales lift = discount% / (CM ratio - discount%). Worked shape: at a 0.5 CM ratio a 20% discount needs sales to rise 20/(50-20) = 67% just to break even; at a 0.4 CM ratio the same 20% off needs a 100% lift. Most promos do not clear that bar, so discounting usually destroys contribution unless it is a deliberate acquisition or clearance spend. This is arithmetic [FACT-managerial-accounting]; the elasticity that says whether the lift is achievable is [UNKNOWN] until tested.

included: discount comes entirely out of contribution
break-even lift = discount/(CM ratio - discount)
worked lift figures at sample CM ratios

pros.claim: The break-even-lift identity exposes that modest discounts demand implausible volume, disciplining promo decisions
pros.example: showing a 20% discount needs a 67% sales lift at a 0.5 CM ratio kills most casual markdowns

cons.claim: The identity gives the required lift but not the achievable lift, which depends on [UNKNOWN] elasticity
cons.example: a genuinely elastic hero SKU might clear the bar, which the arithmetic alone cannot confirm

failure_modes: reading a small % discount as a small margin hit and under-estimating the required volume lift
assuming the break-even lift is achievable without an elasticity test
acceptance_tests: the discount-comes-from-contribution point and the break-even lift = discount/(CM ratio - discount) identity are stated with worked lift figures at sample CM ratios, and achievability flagged as [UNKNOWN] elasticity
revisit_triggers: a promo elasticity/lift result lands
the CM ratio changes and re-computes the break-even lift
a clearance or acquisition promo is proposed

base.update_signal: a promo elasticity result or a CM ratio change updates the break-even lift

nodes.definition: Carry the non-arithmetic damage discounting does and the legal guardrail on it. Beyond the immediate contribution loss, repeated promotions (1) reset the customer's reference price so the discounted price becomes the expected price and perceived value erodes, (2) train buyers to wait for the next sale (promo dependency), and (3) can cheapen the brand's quality signal, undoing the perceived-value work. The owner's poll-with-free-item incentive is a related lever whose response inflation must not be read as WTP (S4). Legal guardrail [FACT]: FTC Guides Against Deceptive Pricing (16 CFR Part 233) require any 'was/now', 'list price' or comparative-price claim to reference a bona fide former or prevailing price actually offered; a fictitious former price to manufacture a discount is deceptive. So a defensible price is best held by value engineering, not perpetual discounting.

included: reference-price erosion and promo dependency
brand quality-signal damage from perpetual sales
FTC 16 CFR 233 former-price rule [FACT]

pros.claim: Naming reference-price erosion and the FTC rule stops discounting from silently destroying perceived value or crossing a legal line
pros.example: avoiding a perpetual 'was $50 now $30' that no one ever paid keeps both perceived value and 16 CFR 233 compliance intact

cons.claim: The erosion and brand-damage effects are directional [ESTIMATE]s, hard to quantify per promo
cons.example: one launch promo may not measurably erode reference price, making the risk case judgemental

failure_modes: running perpetual sales that reset the reference price and train buyers to wait
advertising a fictitious former price in violation of FTC 16 CFR 233
acceptance_tests: reference-price erosion, promo dependency, brand-signal damage and the FTC 16 CFR 233 bona-fide-former-price rule are stated as the reasons a defensible price is held by value engineering not perpetual discounting
revisit_triggers: a promo's reference-price/brand effect is measured
an advertised comparative price needs FTC compliance review
the incentive/giveaway plan (S4) changes

base.update_signal: a reference-price/brand-effect measurement or an FTC-compliance question arises

nodes.definition: Operationalise 'lower the price without lowering the quality' as a COGS-reduction job, not a discount. Pull the S2 kb3_quality_cost_value_engineering levers to lower the landed-COGS floor while holding real and perceived quality: base-metal selection (e.g. 316L stainless or 925 vs brass for the same look with different cost/skin-safety), plating micron tuning (enough gold/rhodium thickness to pass adhesion/tarnish/wear tests without gold-flashing waste), barrier/strike layers and e-coat that extend finish life per micron, findings and component standardisation, and batch/MOQ economics that cut per-unit cost. Each lever lowers TARGET_MARGIN_FLOOR, letting DEFENSIBLE_PRICE_METHOD set a lower price at the SAME margin and quality tier - the honest answer to the owner's 'decrease price without decreasing quality'. Quality is protected by holding the S2 acceptance tests (adhesion, tarnish/salt-spray, nickel EN1811 <=0.5 ug/cm2/week) as gates, so cost-down never becomes quality-down.

included: S2 COGS-reduction levers lowering the floor at held quality
quality protected by S2 acceptance tests (adhesion/tarnish/nickel)
value engineering as the honest cost-down-without-quality-down path
excluded: the materials-science derivation of the levers (S2 kb3)

pros.claim: Framing a lower price as value engineering lets the venture cut price permanently without sacrificing margin or quality
pros.example: standardising findings and right-sizing plating micron cuts landed COGS enough to lower the price a tier while passing the same durability tests

cons.claim: Cost-down levers can quietly cross into quality-down if the S2 acceptance tests are not held as hard gates
cons.example: thinning plating below the adhesion/tarnish threshold cuts cost but fails durability and becomes a stealth quality cut

failure_modes: thinning plating or swapping base metal below the S2 durability/nickel gates and calling it value engineering
confusing a value-engineering reprice with a discount and sacrificing margin instead of cost
acceptance_tests: the S2 COGS-reduction levers (base metal, plating micron, barrier layers, findings, batch/MOQ) are shown lowering the floor at held margin, with quality protected by the S2 acceptance tests (adhesion/tarnish/nickel EN1811) as hard gates
revisit_triggers: S2 kb3 updates a cost lever or its durability gate
a plating/base-metal change is proposed for cost reasons
a MOQ/batch economics change alters the achievable floor

base.update_signal: an S2 cost lever, durability gate, or MOQ economics change moves the achievable floor

nodes.definition: The decision rule that classifies any proposed lower price BEFORE acting, because discount and value engineering are opposite operations. Ask: is the goal a temporary demand spike / clearance (then a DISCOUNT is the tool - accept the contribution sacrifice, size the break-even lift, respect FTC former-price rules, time-box it) or a permanently lower competitive price (then a VALUE-ENGINEERING REPRICE is the tool - cut the COGS floor via S2 levers, hold margin and quality, no reference-price erosion)? Default rule: if the lower price must be permanent to win the band, it is a value-engineering job, not a discount; discounting a structurally over-costed SKU just bleeds margin indefinitely. Mis-classification is the core error the owner's 'decrease price without decreasing quality' ask guards against - the answer is almost always value engineering, not a standing discount.

included: the temporary-spike -> discount vs permanent-price -> value-engineer classification
the default that a permanent lower price is a value-engineering job
mis-classification as the core error

pros.claim: A classify-before-acting rule stops a permanent pricing problem from being papered over with a standing discount
pros.example: recognising that a SKU needs to sit a tier lower permanently routes it to value engineering, not a perpetual sale that bleeds margin

cons.claim: Some cases are genuinely mixed (a launch discount while value engineering the next batch), so the rule needs judgement
cons.example: a time-boxed launch promo can coexist with a value-engineering reprice for the restock

failure_modes: running a standing discount on a structurally over-costed SKU that should have been value-engineered
value-engineering a SKU that only needed a short clearance push
acceptance_tests: a proposed lower price is classified as a temporary discount vs a permanent value-engineering reprice before acting, with the default that a permanent competitive price is a value-engineering job not a standing discount
revisit_triggers: a SKU's competitive position requires a permanent price move
a clearance/launch event is proposed
a value-engineering reprice changes the SKU's floor

base.update_signal: a permanent-vs-temporary price situation or a value-engineering result changes the classification

nodes.definition: Separate list contribution from realized contribution so the priced margin survives contact with reality. List/nominal contribution uses the full price; realized contribution nets out returns and exchanges, the refurbishment or write-off cost of returned plated pieces (a returned earring may be unsellable for hygiene reasons; a scratched-plating return may be unrecoverable), inventory shrink, and payment chargebacks/fraud. Realized contribution <= list contribution always. The reserve is carried in VARIABLE_COST_SCOPE and sized per category from measured or estimated return rates (jewelry return/exchange behaviour is category- and fit-dependent; sizing-driven returns for rings link to the S3 form specialist). The reserve is [METHOD/ESTIMATE], measured once the store has data, but never omitted - a price that looks profitable on list margin can be thin or negative on realized margin.

included: list vs realized contribution
returns/refurbish/shrink/chargeback reserve
per-category reserve sizing linked to fit/returns (S3)

pros.claim: Netting returns and shrink into realized margin stops a list-margin-profitable SKU from hiding a realized loss
pros.example: a hygiene-unsellable earring return turns a thin list margin negative once the write-off is booked

cons.claim: Return and shrink rates are [UNKNOWN] pre-launch, so the early reserve is an estimate that can misstate realized margin
cons.example: a guessed 5% return reserve may prove low for a sizing-sensitive ring

failure_modes: pricing on list contribution and ignoring the realized hit from returns and shrink
omitting the refurbish/write-off cost of unsellable returned plated pieces
acceptance_tests: list vs realized contribution is separated, a returns/refurbish/shrink/chargeback reserve is carried per category ([METHOD/ESTIMATE], never omitted), and realized <= list contribution is stated
revisit_triggers: measured return/exchange or shrink rates arrive from the store
a sizing/fit change (S3) alters ring return rates
a chargeback/fraud rate change occurs

base.update_signal: a measured return/shrink/chargeback rate or a fit-driven return change arrives

nodes.definition: Enforce the honesty discipline across the pricing work so firm math is trusted while every market number stays labelled. Solid [FACT] (cited, load-bearing): keystone = 2.0x cost = 50% margin; markup-on-cost vs margin-on-price arithmetic; the contribution-margin and CM-ratio identities; the discount break-even-lift identity; FTC 16 CFR 233 former-price rule; vermeil/rhodium FTC 16 CFR 23 definitions used in the materials story. [METHOD] (a way to obtain a number, not the number): WTP measurement (Van Westendorp/Gabor-Granger/conjoint/A-B), competitor band-mapping from public storefronts, returns-reserve sizing. [UNKNOWN] until produced: the actual WTP/ceiling, specific competitor prices, elasticity, return rates, and therefore the final retail price. Any single retail price stated before measurement is an illustration, not a claim; the fashion-jewelry above-keystone multiple is [ESTIMATE]. This is the same discipline as the sweater landed-cost KB.

included: the [FACT] identities vs the [METHOD] instruments vs the [UNKNOWN] market numbers
single retail prices as illustrations until measured
the above-keystone multiple as [ESTIMATE]
excluded: the substantive pricing content (the other nodes)

pros.claim: A single ledger separating firm math from methods and unknowns keeps the pricing trustworthy without inventing market numbers
pros.example: tagging the CM identity [FACT] but the WTP ceiling [UNKNOWN] tells a reader exactly what to trust

cons.claim: Heavy tagging can frustrate a stakeholder who wants one price the evidence does not yet support
cons.example: someone wanting a single launch price must accept a defensible range until WTP is measured

failure_modes: promoting an illustrative single price to a measured claim
stating a competitor price, WTP or elasticity as fact when it is [UNKNOWN]
acceptance_tests: the [FACT] identities, the [METHOD] instruments and the [UNKNOWN] market numbers are enumerated, single pre-measurement prices are flagged as illustrations, and the above-keystone multiple is tagged [ESTIMATE]
revisit_triggers: a [METHOD] measurement converts an [UNKNOWN] into a labelled figure
a [FACT] identity or FTC rule is revised
a single price is found circulating as a measured claim

base.update_signal: a measurement resolves an unknown or a FACT/FTC anchor is revised

nodes.definition: Compose the segment's hand-off and stop cleanly. Deliver, per SKU: the defensible retail price (a point or a labelled range if WTP is unmeasured), the per-unit contribution-before-marketing and CM ratio at that price, the contribution floor and its required-margin logic, the competitor band placement, the discount policy (time-boxed only, FTC-compliant, no reference-price erosion) and the value-engineering reprice option with its floor impact. This KB owns whether a plated SKU has a defensible price and a positive unit contribution; it does NOT own CAC, AOV, repeat/LTV, payback or break-even units, nor the go/no-go verdict (kb3_viability_cac_ltv), nor the launch-set selection (S5 assortment). The binding conditions it passes on: never price below the contribution floor; measure WTP before hardening a price; hold a lower price by value engineering not standing discounts; carry the realized-margin reserve.

included: per-SKU price + unit contribution-before-marketing + CM ratio + floor + band + discount/VE policy
the clean boundary before CAC/LTV/break-even/assortment
the binding pricing conditions passed to the decision layer

pros.claim: A clean hand-off delivers a defensible price and unit contribution per SKU and names the conditions without overstepping into the viability verdict
pros.example: passing a $29 price with a 0.6 CM ratio, a $15 floor and a value-engineering option lets kb3 run CAC/LTV on a sound contribution base

cons.claim: The hand-off is a contribution-before-marketing figure, so the viability layer inherits a number that CAC can still turn negative
cons.example: a healthy 0.6 CM ratio can still fail once kb3 loads a high paid-social CAC

failure_modes: letting the priced contribution drift into a go/no-go verdict this segment does not own
handing off a single hardened price instead of the range plus floor/band/discount conditions when WTP is unmeasured
acceptance_tests: the per-SKU price, unit contribution-before-marketing, CM ratio, floor, band, and discount/value-engineering policy are delivered with the clean pre-CAC boundary and the four binding conditions (never below floor, measure WTP, value-engineer not discount, carry the returns reserve)
revisit_triggers: a pricing input (floor, WTP, band, COGS) is updated
kb3 requests a tighter price or contribution figure
a value-engineering reprice or discount-policy change occurs

base.update_signal: a pricing input or a downstream request changes the hand-off

edges.why_related: the landed COGS is the cost the keystone multiple is applied to as a floor check
the keystone 2x is the worked example the markup-vs-margin arithmetic disambiguates
margin-on-price is the base the contribution-margin ratio is defined on
landed COGS is the core component of the variable cost the CM identity subtracts
the CM identity requires the variable-cost term it scopes
DTC capture is framed as retaining the keystone spreads a reseller chain would take
the perceived-value market structure is what makes value-based pricing the right method
the WTP the value levers move is what the measurement instruments quantify
the value story determines which competitor tier band the SKU can defensibly sit in
the band sets the range the charm-priced point is chosen inside
the required CM ratio defines the contribution floor price
the variable cost is the numerator of the floor-price formula

the competitor band is the tier constraint the method prices inside
the measured WTP band supplies the ceiling the method uses

the floor>ceiling branch of the price method triggers the value-engineering reprice
the decision classifies a price cut as a margin-sacrificing discount using its contribution math
the decision classifies a permanent price cut as a value-engineering reprice
realized contribution nets returns and shrink out of the list contribution identity
the price method's bounds are what the ledger tags as FACT/METHOD/UNKNOWN
the unmeasured WTP is the core [UNKNOWN] the ledger enumerates

cost-plus keystone and perceived-value pricing give different prices for the same piece, tempting a single cost-based rule
edges.resolution_rule: use keystone/cost-plus only as the floor sanity check and set the actual price on perceived value bounded below by the contribution floor; never let the cost multiple be the final price for a fashion accessory

edges.why_related: the WTP ceiling can sit below the contribution floor, so pricing to value would lose money
edges.resolution_rule: if the WTP ceiling is below the contribution floor, do not price into loss: trigger a value-engineering reprice to lower the floor or drop the SKU; the floor always wins over the ceiling

edges.why_related: tactical discounting pulls price below the defensible floor-ceiling-band price for a demand spike
edges.resolution_rule: hold the defensible price as the reference; permit only time-boxed, FTC-compliant discounts that never breach the contribution floor, and route permanent price needs to value engineering

edges.why_related: a permanent lower price can be reached either by value engineering (cut COGS, hold margin) or by a standing discount (sacrifice margin), which are opposite operations
edges.resolution_rule: for any permanent price reduction default to value engineering; use a standing discount only for genuine time-boxed clearance, per the classify-before-acting rule

edges.why_related: repeated promotions to drive volume erode the reference price and quality signal the value levers built
edges.resolution_rule: protect perceived value: cap promo frequency, keep an FTC-bona-fide former price, and prefer value engineering over perpetual discounting to hold a lower price

edges.why_related: the inherited landed COGS band caps how low the contribution floor can go before value engineering
the returns/shrink reserve raises the variable cost and therefore lifts the floor

conflict_axes.name: cost_plus_keystone_vs_perceived_value
conflict_axes.description: A cost multiple (keystone/markup) gives a fast defensible floor but a fashion accessory's defensible price is set by perceived value, which is usually far higher; leading on either alone misprices.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use keystone/cost-plus as the floor sanity check and set the price on perceived value bounded below by the contribution floor

conflict_axes.name: wtp_ceiling_vs_contribution_floor
conflict_axes.description: The most customers will pay can sit below the price that earns the required margin, so pricing to value and covering cost can be incompatible for a SKU.
poles: price down to the WTP ceiling
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the floor always wins; if WTP < floor, value-engineer the COGS to lower the floor or drop the SKU, never price into loss

conflict_axes.name: discount_vs_defensible_price_integrity
conflict_axes.description: A tactical discount lifts short-term volume but pulls price below the defensible floor-ceiling-band price and can breach the contribution floor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the defensible price as reference; allow only time-boxed FTC-compliant discounts that never breach the contribution floor

conflict_axes.name: discount_vs_value_engineering_reprice
conflict_axes.description: A permanent lower price can come from cutting COGS (value engineering, holds margin and quality) or from a standing discount (sacrifices margin); they are opposite operations that are easily confused.
poles: cut price via a standing discount
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default any permanent price reduction to value engineering; reserve standing discounts for genuine time-boxed clearance

conflict_axes.name: cost_down_vs_quality_down
conflict_axes.description: Value-engineering levers (thinner plating, cheaper base metal) lower COGS but can cross into a stealth quality cut if durability and skin-safety gates are not held.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the S2 acceptance tests (adhesion, tarnish/salt-spray, nickel EN1811) as hard gates; a cost lever that fails a gate is a quality cut, not value engineering

conflict_axes.name: list_margin_vs_realized_margin
conflict_axes.description: A price can look profitable on list contribution yet be thin or negative on realized contribution once returns, refurbishment and shrink are netted out.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry a per-category returns/refurbish/shrink reserve in variable cost so the price clears realized, not just list, contribution

conflict_axes.name: gross_margin_vs_after_cac_reality
conflict_axes.description: The high DTC captured-spread gross margin looks like profit, but CAC (owned by kb3) is subtracted from it, so contribution-before-marketing can still fail after acquisition cost.
poles: reserve for the CAC that eats it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat contribution-before-marketing as a pool CAC is paid from; set the required CM ratio (and floor) high enough to reserve for CAC before pricing

conflict_axes.name: measured_price_vs_invented_number
conflict_axes.description: Stakeholders want a single retail/competitor/WTP price now, but the evidence supports only a labelled band or an [UNKNOWN] until a survey, A/B test or public pull is run.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the band and label any single pre-measurement price an illustration; convert [UNKNOWN] to a figure only via a named [METHOD]

conflict_axes.name: charm_point_vs_hard_constraints
conflict_axes.description: A psychologically optimal price ending (e.g. $.99) can pull the chosen point away from the floor/ceiling/band intersection.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tune the last digit only within the feasible intersection; a charm ending never justifies breaching the contribution floor

edge_cases.description: A SKU's measured willingness-to-pay ceiling sits below its contribution floor, so no defensible margin-earning price exists
edge_cases.trigger: WTP ceiling < contribution floor for a SKU
edge_cases.mitigation: value-engineer the COGS to lower the floor or drop the SKU; never discount into loss to bridge the gap

edge_cases.description: A permanent price cut needed to win the band is run as a standing discount instead of a value-engineering reprice, bleeding margin indefinitely
edge_cases.trigger: a structurally over-costed SKU is put on a perpetual sale rather than re-engineered
edge_cases.mitigation: classify before acting; route a permanent competitive price to value engineering and reserve discounts for time-boxed clearance

edge_cases.description: A cost-down lever thins plating or swaps base metal below the durability/skin-safety gate and is mislabelled value engineering
edge_cases.trigger: plating micron cut below adhesion/tarnish threshold or a nickel-releasing base metal introduced to cut cost
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the S2 acceptance tests (adhesion, tarnish/salt-spray, nickel EN1811 <=0.5 ug/cm2/week) as hard gates; a lever that fails a gate is a quality cut

edge_cases.description: A margin target is expressed as a markup on cost and applied as if it were a margin on price, systematically under-pricing
edge_cases.trigger: a 'X% markup' set as if it were an 'X% margin'
edge_cases.mitigation: convert the target margin to the correct cost multiple (price = cost/(1-margin)) before setting the floor

edge_cases.description: A small percentage discount is treated as a small margin hit, ignoring that the whole cut comes out of contribution
edge_cases.trigger: a promo sized without the break-even-lift math
edge_cases.mitigation: compute required lift = discount/(CM ratio - discount) and only run the promo if that lift is plausibly achievable

edge_cases.description: A competitor or WTP price is invented to fill a band rather than pulled from dated public listings or a measurement
edge_cases.trigger: a price stated as fact without a public pull or survey behind it
edge_cases.mitigation: pull and date public competitor listings and mark WTP [UNKNOWN] until measured; never assert an unmeasured price

edge_cases.description: A price looks profitable on list contribution but is thin or negative on realized contribution after returns and refurbishment
edge_cases.trigger: pricing on list margin without a returns/shrink reserve
edge_cases.mitigation: carry a per-category returns/refurbish/shrink/chargeback reserve so the price clears realized contribution

edge_cases.description: An incentivised poll (free item to respond) is read as revealed willingness-to-pay and inflates the WTP ceiling
edge_cases.trigger: a giveaway-incentivised survey response used as a WTP or demand signal
edge_cases.mitigation: treat incentivised stated preference as biased upward; confirm with a revealed-preference A/B price test before hardening a price

edge_cases.description: A perpetual 'was $X now $Y' sale advertises a former price the item was never genuinely offered at
edge_cases.trigger: a comparative/list price used without a bona fide former price
edge_cases.mitigation: comply with FTC 16 CFR 233: reference only a bona fide former or prevailing price; cap promo frequency to protect the reference price

edge_cases.description: The DTC gross margin is read as profit and the SKU is priced without reserving for the CAC that will be subtracted from it
edge_cases.trigger: a price/floor set on gross margin without a CAC reserve in the required CM ratio
edge_cases.mitigation: set the required CM ratio to reserve CAC + overhead + returns + profit so the floor is not below what kb3's CAC needs

edge_cases.description: A charm-priced ending (e.g. $.99) is chosen that falls below the contribution floor
edge_cases.trigger: a psychological price point selected outside the feasible floor/ceiling/band intersection
edge_cases.mitigation: restrict charm/anchoring tuning to the feasible intersection; if no charm point fits, move the band or value-engineer, do not breach the floor

edge_cases.description: A single launch price is hardened before any WTP measurement, over-committing to an unvalidated number
edge_cases.trigger: a pre-launch SKU priced at a single point with WTP still [UNKNOWN]
edge_cases.mitigation: launch with a defensible price range and run a Van Westendorp/A-B test to tighten it before hardening

workflow.action: Accept the inherited landed COGS band
workflow.description: State the per-SKU landed COGS band from kb1 with plating micron / base metal / MOQ as width drivers, as the price floor and CM denominator input
workflow.gate: the per-SKU landed COGS band is stated as accepted input with its width drivers named

workflow.action: Fix the keystone and markup-vs-margin facts
workflow.description: State keystone = 2.0x cost = 50% margin [FACT], the above-keystone fashion multiple [ESTIMATE], and the markup-on-cost vs margin-on-price arithmetic
workflow.gate: keystone [FACT], the [ESTIMATE] fashion multiple, and the markup-vs-margin distinction are stated

workflow.action: Compute the contribution-margin identity and variable-cost scope
workflow.description: State CM = price - variable cost and CM ratio = CM/price [FACT], contribution-before-marketing, and enumerate variable cost (landed COGS + fees + pick/pack + returns reserve)
workflow.gate: the CM identity and the variable-cost scope (CAC/fixed excluded) are stated

workflow.description: State that DTC captures both markup spreads but funds CAC/fulfilment/returns from them, so gross margin is necessary not sufficient
workflow.gate: the captured-spread framing and the necessary-not-sufficient point are stated

workflow.action: Establish perceived-value pricing and WTP measurement
workflow.description: State value-based pricing levers and name the WTP instruments (Van Westendorp/Gabor-Granger/conjoint/A-B) with bias caveats, WTP marked [UNKNOWN] until measured
workflow.gate: the value levers, the [METHOD] WTP instruments, and the bias caveats are stated with WTP [UNKNOWN]

workflow.action: Build the competitor band and price point
workflow.description: Map competitor prices from dated public storefronts into entry/hero/premium tiers and choose a charm-priced point inside the band
workflow.gate: the band is built from dated public listings [METHOD] and a charm point is placed inside it

workflow.description: Compute floor price = variable cost / (1 - required CM ratio) with the required CM ratio reserving CAC + overhead + returns + profit
workflow.gate: the floor price and its required-CM-ratio logic (reserving CAC) are stated as the never-break constraint

workflow.description: Pick a charm-tuned point inside the intersection of floor, WTP ceiling and competitor band; route floor>ceiling to value engineering or drop
workflow.gate: the price sits inside floor/ceiling/band with the floor>ceiling branch routed to value engineering, not a loss-making discount

workflow.action: Compute the discount effect and its traps
workflow.description: State the break-even lift = discount/(CM ratio - discount), reference-price erosion, and the FTC 16 CFR 233 former-price rule
workflow.gate: the break-even-lift math and the reference-price/FTC guardrails are stated

workflow.action: Apply the value-engineering reprice and classify the price cut
workflow.description: Pull S2 COGS levers to lower the floor at held quality and classify any lower price as a temporary discount vs a permanent value-engineering reprice
workflow.gate: the S2 levers lower the floor at held quality gates and any price cut is classified before acting

workflow.action: Net returns into realized margin and enforce the honesty ledger
workflow.description: Separate list vs realized contribution with a returns/shrink reserve, and enumerate the [FACT] identities vs [METHOD] instruments vs [UNKNOWN] market numbers
workflow.gate: realized-vs-list contribution and the FACT/METHOD/UNKNOWN discipline are stated with single prices flagged as illustrations

workflow.description: Deliver per-SKU price, unit contribution-before-marketing, CM ratio, floor, band and discount/VE policy, stopping before CAC/LTV/break-even
workflow.gate: the per-SKU price, contribution, floor, band, discount/VE policy, clean pre-CAC boundary and four binding conditions are stated

dominance_rules.rule: The contribution floor dominates the WTP ceiling and the competitor band
dominance_rules.rationale: a price below the contribution floor loses money on every unit and cannot be fixed by volume
dominance_rules.trigger: a WTP or band target would set a price below the contribution floor
dominance_rules.action: hold the floor; value-engineer the COGS to lower it or drop the SKU, never price into loss

dominance_rules.rule: Perceived-value pricing dominates cost-plus keystone for the final price
dominance_rules.rationale: for a low-ticket fashion accessory material cost is a weak price anchor and cost-plus leaves money on the table
dominance_rules.trigger: a price is set on a cost multiple alone
dominance_rules.action: use keystone only as the floor check and set the price on perceived value bounded below by the floor

dominance_rules.rule: A permanent price reduction is value engineering, not a standing discount
dominance_rules.rationale: cutting COGS holds margin and quality while a standing discount bleeds margin indefinitely
dominance_rules.trigger: a SKU needs a permanently lower price to compete
dominance_rules.action: value-engineer the COGS floor via S2 levers; reserve discounts for time-boxed clearance

dominance_rules.rule: The quality/durability gate dominates any cost-down lever
dominance_rules.rationale: a cost cut that fails adhesion/tarnish/nickel tests is a quality cut, not value engineering
dominance_rules.trigger: a plating-micron or base-metal change is proposed to cut cost
dominance_rules.action: hold the S2 acceptance tests as hard gates; reject any lever that fails them

dominance_rules.rule: Realized contribution dominates list contribution for pricing decisions
dominance_rules.rationale: returns, refurbishment and shrink make realized margin the one the business actually earns
dominance_rules.trigger: a price is justified on list margin alone
dominance_rules.action: carry a returns/shrink reserve and require the price to clear realized contribution

dominance_rules.rule: Margin-on-price dominates markup-on-cost as the base for contribution math
dominance_rules.rationale: the CM ratio is defined on price and mixing bases systematically under-prices
dominance_rules.trigger: a target is expressed as a markup and used as a margin
dominance_rules.action: convert to the price base (price = cost/(1-margin)) before computing the floor

dominance_rules.rule: The CAC reserve dominates the raw DTC gross margin
dominance_rules.rationale: contribution-before-marketing is a pool CAC is subtracted from, so a high gross margin is not profit
dominance_rules.trigger: a floor or price is set on gross margin without reserving for CAC
dominance_rules.action: set the required CM ratio to reserve CAC + overhead + returns + profit before pricing

dominance_rules.rule: A named measurement dominates an asserted price
dominance_rules.rationale: any WTP/competitor/retail price is [UNKNOWN] until a survey, A/B test or public pull produces it
dominance_rules.trigger: a single market price is stated as fact pre-measurement
dominance_rules.action: carry a labelled band and convert [UNKNOWN] to a figure only via a named [METHOD]

dominance_rules.rule: FTC bona-fide former-price rule dominates a manufactured discount
dominance_rules.rationale: advertising a fictitious former price violates FTC 16 CFR 233
dominance_rules.trigger: a 'was/now' or list-price comparison lacks a genuine former price
dominance_rules.action: reference only a bona fide former or prevailing price, or drop the comparative claim

anti_rework_rules.rule: Convert every margin target to the price base before setting any floor or price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a markup-as-margin under-pricing error propagated through the whole price model and corrected late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute the contribution floor (reserving CAC) before choosing a WTP/band price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: setting an attractive price that later proves below the margin-earning floor and must be re-raised

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark every WTP, competitor and retail price [UNKNOWN] until a named method produces it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an invented price circulating as a measured claim and having to be retracted downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify a proposed lower price as discount vs value-engineering reprice before acting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: papering a permanent cost problem with a standing discount that bleeds margin and must be unwound

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the S2 durability/nickel acceptance tests as gates on any cost-down lever from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stealth quality cut shipped as value engineering that triggers returns and brand damage

anti_rework_rules.rule: Carry a returns/refurbish/shrink reserve in variable cost from the first price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: pricing on list margin and discovering a realized-margin loss after returns are booked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size any discount with the break-even-lift math before running it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a promo that destroys contribution because the required volume lift was never achievable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep contribution-before-marketing labelled and reserve CAC in the floor from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: handing a gross-margin-healthy price to kb3 that CAC turns negative, forcing a re-price

iteration_protocol.trigger: kb1 republishes the landed COGS band or a value-engineering reprice lowers COGS
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the contribution floor and the defensible price for every affected SKU

iteration_protocol.trigger: a WTP survey or live A/B price test completes
iteration_protocol.action: replace the [UNKNOWN] WTP ceiling with the measured band and tighten the defensible price

iteration_protocol.trigger: kb3 measures or revises CAC and the required CM ratio
iteration_protocol.action: re-set the required CM ratio, recompute the floor, and re-check every price against it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fresh public competitor price pull is run
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the price band and re-place the SKU's price point

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured return/exchange or shrink rates arrive from the store
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the returns reserve and update realized contribution and the floor

iteration_protocol.trigger: a promo or standing discount is proposed
iteration_protocol.action: run the break-even-lift math, classify discount vs value engineering, and check FTC former-price compliance

iteration_protocol.trigger: an S2 cost lever or durability/nickel gate is updated
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the value-engineering reprice and its floor impact against the held quality gates

priority_rationale: The inherited landed COGS, the keystone/markup-vs-margin facts and the fashion-jewelry price structure come first because every margin number depends on the correct cost base, the price-vs-cost arithmetic and the perceived-value framing; the contribution-margin identity, variable-cost scope, DTC capture, perceived-value levers, WTP measurement and competitor band next, because they are the floor and ceiling inputs; the contribution floor and the defensible-price method then synthesise floor-ceiling-band into a price; the discount effect, promo trap, value-engineering link and discount-vs-VE decision handle lowering price honestly; and the realized-margin, honesty-ledger and hand-off nodes come last because they protect the priced margin, enforce the FACT/METHOD/UNKNOWN discipline and compose the clean boundary before the CAC/LTV viability layer.
